question.leadin: Answer some questions about the presidency of John F. Kennedy.
question.text: The Kennedy administration approved this failed 1961 invasion of Cuba led by Cuban exiles, which increased tensions, leading to the Cuban Missile Crisis.
question.clue: This event's failure led Allen Dulles to be forced to resign.

swap.leadin: Before dying in a plane crash, Ted Stevens described this technology as a "series of tubes" in a hearing about its namesake neutrality.
swap.text: Name this technology. Al Gore was misquoted as saying he "invented" this technology in a CNN interview, when in reality he was referring to his support of the High Performance Computing Act.
swap.answerHtml: Internet [accept the World Wide Web; prompt on network; prompt on network neutrality; prompt on technology or IT or software]
swap.clue: Companies centered on this technology primarily drove the high growth of the NASDAQ in the 1990s. Senator Ted Stevens oddly described this technology as a "series of tubes."

question.leadin: Answer the following about conflict in the Balkans.
question.text: This U.S. president ordered those bombings, but is probably better known for playing the saxophone and having a sex scandal.
question.clue: With his wife and the McDougals, this man was involved in a failed business venture called Whitewater, and he was investigated by independent counsel Kenneth Starr.

swap.text: Clinton's victory in the 1992 election has been linked to this third-party candidate, whose campaign drew voters away from Bush. This billionaire owner of Electronic Data Systems died in 2019.
swap.answerHtml: Ross Perot (accept Henry Ross Perot; accept Henry Ray Perot)
swap.clue: This man promised there would be a "giant sucking sound" as jobs went to Mexico when speaking out against NAFTA.

question.text: The Catcher in the Rye was also found in this man's possession after he fired a rifle from the sixth floor of the Texas School Book Depository.
question.clue: This man's wife Marina photographed him in the backyard holding Marxist newspapers and a rifle.

swap.text: After the invasion, the US passed a bill named for Nichols and this politician to reduce inter-service rivalry. Reagan spoke in support of this conservative politician at the 1964 RᐧNᐧC in the speech "A Time for Choosing".
swap.clue: He was harmed by a message which ended "We must love one another, or we must die" after zooming in on the eye of a figure who skips the number six and repeats the number nine twice in trying to count to ten.

question.leadin: In this event, the Maddox and Turner Joy were attacked by enemy torpedo boats.
question.text: Name this 1964 "incident" that prompted the U.S. to ramp up its involvement in the Vietnam War.
question.clue: This event, which shared its name with a French protectorate, began when the USS Maddox fired warning shots at torpedo boats commanded by Le Duy Khoai.

swap.text: During the McClellan Committee hearings, the Teamsters Union was expelled from this larger union. This union was created from the 1955 merger of two smaller unions led by George Meany and Walter Reuther.
swap.answerHtml: AFL-CIO [or American Federation of Labor and Congress of Industrial Organizations; reject partial answers such as “AFL” and “CIO”]
swap.clue: Before the shots, Reagan had just spoken to a group within this federation of organizations. It kicked out the Teamsters after George Meany and Walter Reuther negotiated to form it in the 50s.

question.text: Brzezinski and Vance both served under this Democratic president, on whose watch the Iran hostage crisis started.
question.clue: After Love Canal was declared a federal emergency area, this man signed the Superfund Law.

swap.leadin: Don DeLillo described this document as "the megaton novel that James Joyce would have written if he'd moved to Iowa City and lived to be a hundred."
swap.text: Identify this government-produced report on the JFK assassination, named for a Chief Justice of the Supreme Court.
swap.clue: John Cooper was joined in this group by the president of the World Bank, John McCloy, while James Lee Rankin served as their General Counsel.

question.leadin: In 1968, things got much more difficult for protesting hippies when they decided to take on the man.
question.text: Originally peaceful anti-war protests turned into a violent police riot thanks to Richard Daley's goons at this event.
question.clue: One of these events saw competition between mostly Catholic "wets" and Protestant "drys"; that one of these events is nicknamed the "Klanbake" due to prominent participation of the KKK.

swap.leadin: Part of the impetus for this policy was the description of the Soviet state by George Kennan in the Long Telegram.
swap.text: Name this foreign policy strategy by President Harry Truman that sought to check the expansion of communism. The Truman Doctrine was the first expression of this greater policy framework.
swap.clue: Alternate strategies to this policy were isolationism, detente and rollback.

question.leadin: Answer the following about shameful US immigration Laws.
question.text: This immigration program initiated under the Eisenhower administration saw the predecessor to ICE deport over 1 Million Mexican Immigrants over 8 years.
question.clue: INS Commissioner Joseph Swing masterminded this initiative that rounded up illegal Mexican immigrants during the Eisenhower administration. It culminated in deportations aboard the ships Emancipation and Mercurio.

swap.leadin: Justice Potter Stewart, who coined the phrase "I know it when I see it" about this kind of material, was asked by a clerk whether he had ever, in fact, seen it, to which he responded "just once, off the coast of Algeria."
swap.text: Name this type of material, defined in a 1973 case as material lacking "serious literary, artistic, political, or scientific value."
swap.clue: The "public good" defence introduced into law through a Roy Jenkins bill was tested in a trial for this offence at which Mervyn Griffith-Jones cross-examined the Bishop of Woolwich.

question.leadin: Following a 1970s civil war, many people of this ethnicity settled in the communities of Eau Claire and Wausau, Wisconsin.
question.text: Name this ethnicity of nearly 400,000 Americans, many of whom came to the US after a "Secret War." In the 1980s, people of this ethnicity relocated from refugee camps to Merced.
question.answerHtml: Hmong Americans [or Hmoob Mes Kas; prompt on Miao, though this term is considered a pejorative)

swap.leadin: Aldrich Ames worked in the counterintelligence division of this agency while he conducted espionage for the Soviet Union.
swap.text: Identify this American spy agency that chased after false Soviet leads at its facility at Warrenton while Ames continued to work at its headquarters in Langley, Virginia.
swap.clue: During the 1980s, this agency was led by William Casey, who may have admitted on his deathbed that he knew about diverting funds to the Contras in Nicaragua.

question.leadin: Its formation was presaged by Truman's decision to desegregate the armed forces and it was made official in 1948 after the passage of a civil rights platform.
question.text: Identify this third party that met in Birmingham, Alabama, to nominate Strom Thurmond for President.
question.answer: Dixiecrats or States' Rights Democratic Party
question.clue: Members had earlier walked out of another party's convention after a speech by Hubert Humphrey.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the career of Senator Joe McCarthy.
swap.text: This notable hack co-wrote McCarthy and His Enemies with brother-in-law William F. Buckley, but is best known for ghostwriting Barry Goldwater's The Conscience of a Conservative.

question.text: After the Great Peruvian Earthquake of 1970 triggered history's deadliest avalanche, the Velasco regime received the personal aid of this woman during their relief efforts. This woman and her husband had earlier been spit on and pelted with rocks during their visit to Venezuela.
question.answerHtml: Pat Nixon [or Thelma Nixon or Thelma Catherine Ryan; prompt on just Nixon] '

swap.leadin: Identify these Supreme Court decisions from descriptions.
swap.text: The Smith Act of 1940, making it a crime to belong to organizations advocating the violent overthrow of the government, was upheld, effectively destroying the Communist Party as a major force in U.S. politics. The "gravity of the evil" allowed for the "clear and present danger" doctrine to be overlooked.
swap.clue: The plurality opinion by Justice Vinson relies on Learned Hand's language weighing whether the "the gravity of the evil, discounted by its improbability" will justify invasion of free speech.
